draft.title: Mean, median and variance of a continuous variable
card: For a pdf f(x), the mean is E(X) = ∫ x f(x) dx, taken over the values X can take. It is the balance point of the distribution.
The median m splits the area under f into two halves. Solve ∫ f(x) dx = 1/2, from the lowest value of X up to m.
Var(X) = E(X²) − [E(X)]², where E(X²) = ∫ x² f(x) dx. The standard deviation is the square root of the variance.
Let f(x) = 2x for 0 ≤ x ≤ 1. Mean = ∫ 2x² dx = 2/3. Median: x² = 1/2, so m = √2/2. E(X²) = ∫ 2x³ dx = 1/2, so Var(X) = 1/2 − 4/9 = 1/18.
draft.remember: Mean uses x times f(x). Median uses half the area. Variance is E(X²) minus the mean squared.

a.q: X has pdf f(x) = 3x² for 0 ≤ x ≤ 1, and 0 otherwise. What is E(X)?
a.why: E(X) = ∫ x · 3x² dx from 0 to 1 = [3x⁴/4] = 3/4. The value 3/5 is tempting, but it comes from ∫ x² · 3x² dx, which is E(X²), not the mean.
a.clue: Multiply f(x) by x before you integrate.

b.q: The time T hours that Priya spends on a task has pdf f(t) = t/2 for 0 ≤ t ≤ 2, and 0 otherwise. What is the median of T?
b.why: Solve ∫ t/2 dt from 0 to m = m²/4 = 1/2, so m² = 2 and m = √2. The value 4/3 is the mean, found with ∫ t · t/2 dt. The value 1 is the middle of the range, but the area is not split evenly there.
b.clue: Set the area from 0 to m equal to 1/2, then solve for m.

check.summary: No problems found. The card example, both answers (E(X) = 3/4 and median √2) and the explanations of the distractors all check out.

final.title: Mean, median and variance of a continuous variable
card: For a pdf \(f(x)\), the mean is \(E(X) = \int x f(x) \, dx\), taken over the values \(X\) can take. It is the balance point of the distribution.
The median \(m\) splits the area under \(f\) into two halves. Solve \(\int_{a}^{m} f(x) \, dx = \frac{1}{2}\), where \(a\) is the lowest value of \(X\).
\(\text{Var}(X) = E(X^{2}) - [E(X)]^{2}\), where \(E(X^{2}) = \int x^{2} f(x) \, dx\). The standard deviation is the square root of the variance.

4.alt: The density \(f(x) = 2x\) for \(0 \le x \le 1\). The median \(m = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \approx 0.71\) splits the area under the line into two halves: the shaded triangle on the left has area \(\frac{1}{2}\), and the part on the right has area \(\frac{1}{2}\).

final.remember: Mean uses \(x\) times \(f(x)\). Median uses half the area. Variance is \(E(X^{2})\) minus the mean squared.

a.q: \(X\) has pdf \(f(x) = 3x^{2}\) for \(0 \le x \le 1\), and 0 otherwise. What is \(E(X)\)?
a.why: \(E(X) = \int_{0}^{1} x \cdot 3x^{2} \, dx = \left[\frac{3x^{4}}{4}\right]_{0}^{1} = \frac{3}{4}\). The value \(\frac{3}{5}\) is tempting, but it comes from \(\int_{0}^{1} x^{2} \cdot 3x^{2} \, dx\), which is \(E(X^{2})\), not the mean.

b.q: The time \(T\) hours that Priya spends on a task has pdf \(f(t) = \frac{t}{2}\) for \(0 \le t \le 2\), and 0 otherwise. What is the median of \(T\)?
b.why: Solve \(\int_{0}^{m} \frac{t}{2} \, dt = \frac{m^{2}}{4} = \frac{1}{2}\), so \(m^{2} = 2\) and \(m = \sqrt{2}\). The value \(\frac{4}{3}\) is the mean, found with \(\int_{0}^{2} t \cdot \frac{t}{2} \, dt\). The value 1 is the middle of the range, but the area is not split evenly there.
b.clue: Set the area from 0 to \(m\) equal to \(\frac{1}{2}\), then solve for \(m\).
